entries.title: A rare tail separates variance and exponential fluctuation thresholds
entries.statement: For n>=64 let R_n be symmetric +/-1 and B_n an independent Bernoulli variable with p_n=exp(-sqrt(n)). Set X_n=n^{1/3}R_n+(n/4)(B_n-p_n), Y_n=3n/2+X_n. Then EX_n=0, n<=Y_n<=2n, and Var X_n=n^{2/3}+(n^2/16)p_n(1-p_n)~n^{2/3}. For this family define chi_a=inf{a: for some alpha>0, sup_n E exp(alpha|X_n|/n^a)<infinity} and chi_b=sup{b: for some c>0,N, Var X_n>=c n^{2b} for all n>=N}. One has chi_a=1/2 and chi_b=1/3. Thus a pure variance power law and uniform square-root exponential concentration do not by themselves identify the two fluctuation thresholds. Indexing by lattice endpoints with n=ceil(|v|) preserves the gap. This is an abstract random-variable family, not an FPP metric or iid-edge construction, and it does not refute P0110.
entries.proof_text: Independence of R_n and B_n gives the exact variance, whose extra term is negligible relative to n^{2/3}. Since |B_n-p_n|<=B_n+p_n, E exp(|X_n|/sqrt(n))<=exp(n^{-1/6}+(sqrt(n)/4)p_n) [1-p_n+p_n exp(sqrt(n)/4)]. This is uniformly bounded because sqrt(n)p_n<=1/e and p_n exp(sqrt(n)/4)=exp(-3sqrt(n)/4). On B_n=1 one has X_n>=n/8 for n>=64: n^{1/3}<=n/16 and p_n<=1/4. For every a<1/2 and alpha>0 the exponential moment is at least exp(-sqrt(n)+(alpha/8)n^{1-a}), which diverges. Hence the upper threshold is exactly 1/2. The variance asymptotic gives the lower threshold 1/3. Finally |X_n|<=n^{1/3}+n/4<=n/2 establishes the bounded passage-time-like range. Ceil(|v|) and |v| are asymptotically comparable, so the same uniform endpoint thresholds persist.
assumptions: abstract family; no FPP representation asserted
